title: Five-Spice Char Siu–Style Glaze
description: Honey, white miso and five individual spices make a mahogany Cantonese-style barbecue glaze with a soft anise finish.

ingredients.name: coconut aminos
ingredients.note: Use Coconut Secret Original at 90 mg sodium per teaspoon. Low-sodium batch: use 1 tsp total.

ingredients.name: mild white miso
ingredients.note: Use plain white miso, ideally no more than 215 mg sodium per teaspoon. Low-sodium batch: use 1/2 tsp total.

ingredients.name: unsalted dry drinking sherry
ingredients.note: Use drinking sherry, without added salt.

ingredients.name: fresh garlic cloves
ingredients.note: Peel and finely grate unless the step specifies otherwise.

ingredients.name: finely ground Sichuan peppercorn husks
ingredients.note: Use a fine seedless grind for a gentle citrus aroma.

steps.title: Warm the five spices
steps.text: Stir {ci}, {ani}, {fe}, {cl} and {sz} over low heat for 20 seconds, just until fragrant.

steps.title: Loosen the paste
steps.text: Whisk {w}, {mis} and {to} into the warm skillet until smooth.

steps.title: Develop the lacquer
steps.text: Stir in {ho}, {a}, {sh} and {ga}. Simmer gently for 6–8 minutes, stirring around the edges to keep the honey from sticking.

steps.title: Mix the slurry
steps.text: Stir {sl} into {cw} in a small cup until smooth.

steps.title: Thicken the sauce
steps.text: Whisk the slurry into the gently simmering base. Cook for 60–90 seconds, stirring, until the sauce coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Check the yield
steps.text: Measure the sauce in a heatproof cup. Aim for 1 cup. If short, loosen with a little hot sodium-free water. If over, return it to the pan and simmer briefly to the mark.

steps.title: Serve the sauce
steps.text: Brush over already-cooked pork or chicken, then spoon a second coat over each portion at the table.

notes: Yield: 1 cup, or four 1/4-cup portions. Low-sodium option for the full batch: Use 1 tsp coconut aminos in place of 4 tsp. Use 1/2 tsp mild white miso in place of 1 tsp. Use the same final 1-cup yield and 1/4-cup serving. Make ahead: Make the sauce the day before and portion it before chilling. Refrigerate in shallow covered portions within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Freeze flat in 1/4-cup portions for up to 2 months. Whisk again after thawing to restore the texture. Fridge reheat: Reheat a portion in a small pan, stirring to a brief boil and at least 165°F. Loosen with a splash of water if it tightens. Freezer reheat: Thaw overnight in the refrigerator, then use the fridge reheat method. Option A uses the listed seasonings. For a gentler Option B, leave out the Sichuan pepper and cloves and replace the sherry with water. Nutrition counts the full sherry before simmering. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/4 of recipe): 59 kcal, 0.5 g protein, 13.1 g total carbohydrate, 0.1 g fat, 0.4 g fiber, 147 mg sodium. Low-sodium version per 1/4 cup: 54 kcal, 0.4 g protein, 11.9 g total carbohydrate, 0.1 g fat, 0.4 g fiber, 53 mg sodium. Figures cover the sauce alone. Sodium varies with brands.
